aions_core/AIONS_ULTIMATE_UNIFIED.py.why: It is the top-level wiring that loads every component and routes a question math-then-facts-then-knowledge, not any one of the search or encoding parts it calls.

aions_core/aions_agent_layer.py.why: Its point is the tool whitelist, risk ratings, per-session quotas and confirmation before anything runs, not the day-to-day skills library itself.

aions_core/server/codebook_engine.py.why: It is the codebook dictionary that swaps phrases for numbered symbols both ways, not a search over stored material.

aions_core/test_aions_capabilities.py.why: It fires personal, emotional and philosophical questions at the live system to see if it can hold that kind of conversation, rather than grading factual support.

control_plane/cbms_gate.py.why: It scores candidate chunks four ways and decides whether the hit is good enough or a model must be paid for, which is the search-and-rank act, not the model machinery.

control_plane/operator/__init__.py.why: A package marker that publishes the observe-diagnose-act-verify-learn loop, so it belongs with live health and self-repair rather than job planning.

control_plane/skills/context.py.why: This is the shared scratchpad of small helper powers handed to each running skill, not the permission decision about whether the skill may run.

control_plane/skills/gate.py.why: It turns destructive skills away without a valid approval and writes every decision to an append-only log, which is permission and risk, not execution.

control_plane/skills/registry.py.why: Dropping a skill.json folder in is enough to make it findable by plain-words search, which is the library itself rather than the gate that vets it.

mcpServers/VS_CODE_MCP_CODEX/src/llm_mou.why: Its job is to voice supplied facts in the user's language without adding any, which is phrasing; the Ollama/GGUF fallback is the secondary concern.

scripts/aions_healthcheck.sh.why: It sweeps services, indexer and API to say up or degraded right now, rather than doing the installation work verify_python_env performs.

scripts/demo_windows_batch2.py.why: A runnable chain of folder, clipboard, screenshot and browser steps meant to show the skills engine working end to end, not the engine itself.

scripts/operator_daily_brief.py.why: It prints the owner's cases, deadlines and goals as a one-page morning summary; the optional health flag is incidental.

scripts/sync_dev_mirror.sh.why: Mirroring the live tree to a dev copy with venv and cache folders left out is groundwork plumbing, not a survey of what is on the drives.

aions_core/aions_reactor.py.why: It drives multi-round learning goals and turns the results into reusable blocks, which is self-improvement rather than the everyday skills library.

aions_core/aions_style_parameters.py.why: Formality, brevity and warmth dials change how a reply reads without touching the facts, so it is tone and not answer quality.

aions_core/server/cbms_purgatory.py.why: It shuffles chunk files between purgatory, active and quarantine folders and keeps the ledger, which is on-disk bookkeeping, not deciding which chunk answers a question.

aions_core/server/crla_core.py.why: Eight candidates scored on coverage, latency and hygiene then run off in a bracket is quality judging, not the retrieval that produced the material.

aions_core/tools/check_schema.py.why: It dumps the tables and columns of the scan database so you can see what was inventoried, which sits with the drive survey tooling, not the vector store.

aions_core/tools/facts_builder.py.why: It walks folders of documents and notes and turns them into indexed one-sentence facts, which is intake, not the later searching over them.

control_plane/planner.py.why: It breaks a stated intent into numbered steps and picks which node runs them, the command centre job rather than the assistant's own answering front door.

control_plane/skills/forge.py.why: This is the request-check-compile-sandbox-promote pipeline for brand-new abilities, not the running of already-approved ones.

control_plane/skills/world_state.py.why: It is the live note of what is currently open or running so a skill is not repeated pointlessly, not a health monitor of services.

mcpServers/VS_CODE_MCP_CODEX/src/desktop.why: It is the actual screen, keyboard and window control ability, not the tool server plumbing that exposes it to an assistant.

scripts/demo_train.py.why: Three scripted scenarios showing planning before and after a recipe is learned; it is the tryout, not the learning machinery it exercises.

scripts/demo_windows_session.py.why: A full monitored session opening Notepad and typing a poem to show real desktop work end to end, rather than the desktop control layer itself.

scripts/hello_world.py.why: The trivial script for confirming a fresh Python environment or harness runs at all, not a demonstration of the system doing a job.

scripts/register_treasure_chunk.py.why: It creates a chunk file and updates the manifest index, which is the storage bookkeeping; the drive catalogue it registers is only its input.
